title: MakeUGC vs Hiring an Agency to Make AI UGC Ads for Your Brand
summary: MakeUGC vs hiring an agency for AI UGC: compare published plans, managed options, trial and refund terms, and who checks each ad, as of October 2026.
body_markdown:
## Which providers should you compare?


### Knowlify: our top pick for done-for-you AI UGC


Knowlify is the best fit when the hours, not the software price, are what you are trying to remove. It delivers about 25 finished ads a week for Facebook and Instagram in three formats: AI UGC with presenters talking to camera, 3D and stylized character animation, and AI commercials. The first batch lands on day five, and a person checks every ad before delivery, so your team receives finished ads rather than renders and retries. You can add end-to-end Meta campaign management or buy creative only.


Pricing is a custom quote with no public rate card. The 90-day guarantee lets you cancel by email for a full refund if the ads have not made more than you paid in that time, with[terms on the site](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) . That 90-day refund applies to creative-only plans; where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month.


When to pick another option: stay with MakeUGC if your team already has the operator, editor and test budget to run self-serve work every week.


### MakeUGC Enterprise: a managed version of the same platform


As of October 2026, MakeUGC's Enterprise page describes Managed by MakeUGC as human-led strategy with AI production on MakeUGC. A creative strategist learns your brand and agrees angles with you, the team generates personas, hooks and scripts, and a strategist reviews every ad before it ships. Finished ads land in a dashboard where you comment, approve and request same-day revisions. The page lists a 48-hour turnaround and 40 to 160 or more videos a month, with a custom retainer and pricing shared on the call.


### Admiral Media: AI UGC batches for apps and ecommerce


As of October 2026, Admiral Media sells creator-style video ads made with AI presenters and finished with human editing and quality review. Starter costs €10,000 for 20 ads of up to 15 seconds, Growth costs €16,000 for 40 ads of up to 30 seconds, and Pro costs €29,000 for 80 ads of up to 60 seconds. Its page says its ideal clients invest US$50,000 or more a month in paid media, and it states that AI UGC is scripted advertising, not content submitted by a real customer.


Choose it when your media budget matches the scale its page describes and you want fixed batches. Campaign and budget management must be agreed separately.


### Pinprick: production paid as a share of ad spend


As of October 2026, Pinprick describes an AI UGC agency for DTC brands that scripts, casts, produces, edits and delivers test-ready ads, with human creative directors reading every frame before it ships. Its pricing page says eligible brands, mainly those already spending meaningfully on ads, pay no per-ad fee. Production is paid as an agreed percentage of ad spend, and the rate is not published.


Choose it when a fee tied to spend fits your model. Ask how eligibility is defined, what counts as spend and what happens if spend falls.


## What should you ask before you sign?


Ask both routes for a finished batch from the same brief, then compare the finished ads rather than renders or credits. A matched test shows you more than any price table.


Ask MakeUGC for the billing period and credit usage on the exact plan you would buy. As of October 2026, its[trial policy](https://makeugc.ai/trial-policy) offers $1 for 72 hours on any plan, though the pricing page says checkout shows the exact length and renewal amount. The trial converts to the standard price unless you cancel in account settings. The $1 fee is non-refundable, and trial output may be watermarked or limited in resolution or length.


Check refund terms before you pay. MakeUGC says fees are generally final, and a discretionary refund request must arrive within three business days of the charge. The amount depends on credits used: a full refund with none used, up to half with less than 50% used, and nothing at 50% or more. Its[refund policy](https://makeugc.ai/refund-policy) sets out the details.


Ask the agency for its guarantee in writing. Knowlify's guarantee is conditional: if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you cancel by email for a full refund under the terms on the site. Managed plans carry an agreed target in 30 days instead.


Ask who writes and approves claims. The FTC's[testimonial guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers) says an AI avatar is prohibited when the testimonial it delivers is fake or false. Its[advertising guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/advertising-faqs-guide-small-business) says advertisers need evidence for their claims. A tool is not evidence that an ad's claims are true, so assign that responsibility whichever route you pick.


Ask how labels will be handled. Meta's[transparency update](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) says it labels ads made with its own generative AI tools when they add a photorealistic AI-generated person, and it plans to detect third-party AI tools and show an "AI info" label in About this ad. Ask each provider which tools touched the render.


If your team can write, render and approve ads every week, MakeUGC's software has the lowest published entry price in this comparison. If you need finished ads on a steady schedule and no production team, compare Knowlify's quote with the managed options above, using the same brief. Our[MakeUGC alternatives guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/makeugc-alternatives) covers more self-serve options.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick for done-for-you AI UGC ads, with a person checking each one, from $5,000 a month.
- MakeUGC is self-serve software with published credit plans, so the production hours stay with your team.
- MakeUGC's Enterprise option is managed on its own platform, which is a closer comparison to an agency than its Starter plan.
- Test both routes with one brief, then compare finished ads and the staff hours each route used.


## FAQ


### Is hiring an agency for AI UGC better than using MakeUGC?


Neither is better in general. Knowlify is our pick for teams that want finished ads without a production team, since it delivers about 25 finished ads a week and checks each one. MakeUGC suits a team that can write, render and approve its own ads on a low monthly plan.


### Is MakeUGC cheaper than an agency?


Its published entry price is lower: Starter is $59 a month billed monthly or $29 billed yearly. Agencies quote per batch or on a custom basis, so the real comparison is finished ads and staff hours. Knowlify's price starts at $5,000 a month, so set it against MakeUGC's plan and your team's hours on a matched brief.


### Does MakeUGC have a free trial?


It offers a $1 trial for 72 hours on any plan. It converts to a paid plan at the standard price unless you cancel in your account settings, and the $1 is non-refundable. Trial output may be watermarked or limited in resolution or length.


### What does MakeUGC Enterprise change?


A creative strategist learns your brand, agrees angles with you and reviews every ad before it ships. Finished ads land in a dashboard for comments and approvals. Its page does not say MakeUGC runs your ad campaigns, so ask that directly before you sign.


### Can Knowlify manage my Meta campaigns as well?


Yes, as an option. Knowlify can run end-to-end Meta campaign management alongside the creative, or deliver creative only for a team with its own media buyer. It does not run TikTok, LinkedIn, Google or YouTube ads.
